lead: Palantir Technologies / PLTR — the growth bill hits the faithful
smaller: Bitcoin / BTC — digital gold fails the war test
DoorDash / DASH — the pandemic habit that stuck
why_lead: Palantir had the largest single-session drop on the card (-15.75% to 11.77 USD, -19.49% over 20 sessions) on a concrete own-date catalyst, Reuters' report that margins will take a hit from higher spending in the commercial push [[n0941]], and it fell on the day the crowd's whole high-beta book sold off (AFRM -12.23%, SHOP -11.63%, SOXL -11.34%, HOOD -9.33%, ARKK -6.44%) as war fear returned (Biden's very-high-risk warning [[n1532]], US calling the withdrawal claim false [[n1528]], VIX +15.73%). Attention evidence comes from the card co-movement of the crowd's tickers including the retail broker itself and from Munger's 'speculative mess' verdict on retail trading apps (Yahoo Finance [[n1869]], Business Insider [[n0869]]); the Smart Money View is genuinely split (Cathie Wood's 'way undervalued' [[n1889]] vs Munger and the Black Swan fund manager's bubble warning [[n1432]]; Temasek adding Robinhood [[n1862]]); the analog pairs the own-date Meta ranking stories (Bloomberg [[n0929]], Business Insider on Tencent replacing it [[n0873]]) with the general spend-now, profit-later repricing mechanism, and Roku's 20% after-hours drop on a revenue miss [[n0949]] shows the same-day intolerance for growth disappointments. Relation to strictly earlier retail notes: Palantir has not appeared in any earlier retail note or draft; the Meta precedent is cited only through the new 17 February market-value ranking stories (Bloomberg, Business Insider), not the crash coverage used on 3, 4 and 8 February. Reviewer change (independent retail review): the intro no longer says Munger's 16 February remarks landed 'the same day' as the 17 February war scare; Bloomberg's Saluzzi segment and its 'ARKK a year from its peak' story were dropped because the 2022-02-17 edition had just used both (replaced by the ARKK card move and the Black Swan manager [[n1432]]); Meta is no longer cited twice for the same point; the Palantir description no longer echoes reference-page wording ('operating system'); the Munich trigger now rests on a clean pre-event Reuters preview [[n0119]] instead of the present-tense 'takes centre stage' item, since the conference opens after the cutoff; Robinhood inferences are framed as market pricing rather than account-level selling.
why_smaller: Bitcoin / BTC: a new crypto narrative, the haven test, on 17 February evidence (separatist shelling [[n1521]]; gold +1.63% to 1,902.00 USD/oz while BTC -7.79% and ETH -7.88%), with Sequoia [[n1067]], Buffett's Nubank stake [[n0828]], the FSB warning [[n1053]] and the Big Short DAO [[n1063]] as the split. Relation to earlier notes: bitcoin led on 8 and 14 February and was a smaller item on 4 February ('the faithful hold while Big Tech bleeds') and 9 February; this edition shows the opposite of the 4 February pattern on new evidence and is kept secondary. Reviewer change: the break level now reads 'the whole rebound since late January', matching the 2022-01-28 reference date, instead of 'the February rebound'. Kept at 171 words as a material update (new 16-17 February evidence), not a brief carryover; it is the edition's only crypto item.

DoorDash / DASH: the pandemic habit that held, with the 17 February session confirming the after-hours beat (CNBC record orders [[n0883]], +10.69% to 105.03 USD). Relation to earlier notes: the 2022-02-17 Shopify lead cited DoorDash's after-hours jump only as a counter-signal; this is the first full item, built on 17 February coverage (n0883, n0884, n0881, n0882, n0853).

Walmart / WMT: the inflation-winner/defensive narrative on its 17 February results (Bloomberg [[n0970]], Modern Retail [[n0971]], NYT [[n0973]], CNBC's shopper warning [[n0974]]), +4.01% on a -2.12% S&P day. Relation to earlier notes: 2022-02-10 ran Chipotle as pricing through inflation and KO as a dividend bunker; Walmart is a different company with a new results catalyst.
considered_not_chosen: Gold / GDX as a separate item (gold 1,902.00 USD/oz, GDX +13.33% over five sessions): gold was a smaller item on 14 and 17 February, so it appears here only as the comparison inside the Bitcoin item.

Roku (revenue miss, shares down 20% after hours [[n0949]]): another growth-miss story close to the Palantir lead and the 17 February Shopify lead, so used only as same-day context in the lead's What Is Driving It rather than as its own item.
Shopify (-11.63%, -26.12% over five sessions) and Affirm (-12.23%): continuations of the 17 and 14 February items, used only as card values in the lead's Social Signal.
Intel investor meeting (NYT comeback question n0960, Fast Company on the $43.5B plan n0911): little price reaction (INTC -1.37%) and no clear crowd angle.
Deere results (Barron's preview 'coming Friday' n0150): pending after the cutoff, not used as a trade thesis.

Not used: n1503 (AP 'US official: Russia adds 7K more troops near Ukraine border', stamped 16 February); for this edition the briefing is before the cutoff, but the BBC report that the US calls the withdrawal claim false [[n1528]] carries the same point. n0156 (Reuters 'Ukraine crisis takes centre stage at Munich Security Conference') and n0157 (NPR on Harris meeting leaders in Munich) are present-tense and may describe the conference after its 18 February opening, so the pending conference is cited through the 14 February Reuters preview [[n0119]]. n1060 (Gadgets 360 'little price movement' in bitcoin and ether) contradicts the completed 17 February daily close and is not used. No item stamped 18 February is used.

Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (+0.39% to 85.49 USD; Reuters on the Trump app opening to hundreds of testers [[n1890]]): the 2022-02-17 smaller item; a tester rollout with a flat price is not a material change, so not repeated.
